notes:
Research. Origin: the issue tree (logic tree, diagnostic tree) is the McKinsey problem-solving staple, formalised in Barbara Minto's Pyramid Principle (the same MECE grouping read top-down as a question rather than as an assertion), popularised in Ethan Rasiel's The McKinsey Way (1999) and given its modern textbook treatment in Conn and McLean, Bulletproof Problem Solving (2018). Two structures share one diagram. An ISSUE TREE decomposes a root question into mutually exclusive, collectively exhaustive sub-questions and stops there; it is a map of what you would have to know. A HYPOTHESIS TREE goes one step further: each branch carries a candidate answer stated so that it could be wrong, plus the analysis that would show it wrong. Hypothesis-driven problem solving (the 'day one answer', the ghost pack) exists to stop the boil-the-ocean data gathering an issue tree alone invites: you do not collect everything, you collect the one observation that kills the most branches. What each slot forces: question forces a single decision-relevant question rather than a topic; issue forces siblings that are MECE, so that no cause hides between branches and no branch is counted twice; hypothesis forces a falsifiable sentence with a direction and a magnitude, not a subject heading; test forces the disconfirming observation, named in advance, with the threshold that would settle it; evidence forces the observation actually in hand, kept separate from the reading of it. Common misuse: hypotheses too vague to be wrong ('marketing is weak'); confirmation-seeking tests that look for supporting data instead of the killer; overlapping or incomplete siblings; the tree used as a work plan (tasks) rather than a logic structure (claims); deep trees that never reach an observation; and prioritising by ease of analysis rather than by which branch, if resolved, most moves the answer. Design consequence for provenance: the test slot is almost always derived, because sources volunteer explanations and almost never volunteer the observation that would kill their own explanation. That contrast is this framework's provenance story: with derived hidden the page shows a question and a heap of volunteered hypotheses with no tests under any of them (a wish list); with derived shown, the MECE issue scaffolding appears above them, the unstated sibling hypotheses appear beside them, and a test hangs under every hypothesis. Scout: launched with Part B plus a framework-specific addendum (what a live diagnostic question looks like, the demand for three or more volunteered candidate answers, quantitative observations that cut both ways, and an explicit warning off two-sided theses and single-chain root-cause narratives, which sibling frameworks own; also excluded the nine episode dates already claimed by sibling agents). It returned three ranked candidates. Chose #1, the 2025-08-09 weekly recap, because the hosts pose the diagnostic question in one sentence out loud, announce that several explanations exist, then volunteer five of them in one continuous segment, each with its own stated connective back to the question, and because the segment contains the rare thing this framework needs: one stated falsification condition. Rejected #2 (2025-09-08 Census AI adoption: excellent contradictory evidence but the root question is mangled in the transcript and the explanations are spread across two distant segments) and #3 (2025-12-10 venture fundraising: strong question, but the candidate answers are mostly speculative futures rather than explanations of the stated anomaly). Design decisions. (1) Kept all five registry slot ids and all four registry relations. Refined two slot descriptions: `hypothesis` typical_provenance is set to 'either' rather than 'derived', because the whole provenance story of this framework is that sources volunteer hypotheses freely (five fact hypotheses in the TBPN example, two in the classic) and never volunteer the test; and `bears_on` is described as running from an observation to a hypothesis or to the question the observation makes a puzzle, so the anomaly evidence can attach to the root. (2) The provenance contrast is deliberately built around the `test` slot: 12 of the 12 tests across both examples are derived except one (t_oai in the TBPN example, quoted verbatim), so hiding the derived layer leaves a question, the volunteered explanations connected by the speakers' own connectives, the evidence, and no way to tell any explanation from any other. That is the wish list the framework exists to replace. (3) The issue layer is entirely derived in both examples and is inserted between the question and the volunteered hypotheses, so the full view shows the MECE scaffolding the source never built. The four TBPN issues are MECE by construction on a ratio: the measurement misassigns work, the numerator genuinely rose, the denominator is capped by supply, the denominator is capped by demand. The demand branch is empty in the source, which is the sharpest single observation the tree produces. (4) idea_bearing_slot is `hypothesis`, with ideas on the two derived hypotheses h_blind (nobody can measure AI revenue) and h_pilot (enterprise AI stuck before production). (5) The classic case is a synthetic profitability diagnostic in the standard consulting form, written so the two volunteered explanations arrive without tests and the source states, in its last sentence, that nobody proposed a way to tell them apart. validate: 0 errors, 0 warnings on the first run. Resume (viz loop). The previous run was killed mid-step-6 and left index.html modified but uncommitted. Inspected it: the extension block is untouched template, the embedded data is byte-identical to graph.json, and `node _meta/build.mjs` reproduces the file exactly, so the modification is nothing but a rebuild against the engine commits that landed after the scaffold (4aca56c derived nodes and legend chips keep their slot shape, afbd828 region captions sit inside their band). No layout work had been done: graph.json is unchanged from the scaffold commit and carries only the levels and slot colour/shape set at scaffold time. The diff touched only engine template code (slot-shaped legend chips and derived-node halos, region captions moved inside their band); the extension block and the embedded data were untouched. So it did not count as viz iteration 1. A second resume (2026-09-09) reset index.html to the scaffold state and ran the builder-critic loop clean from iteration 1. Viz loop resume: the iteration-2 builder was interrupted by a usage limit leaving two uncommitted pos nudges that did not address blocking issue 1; they were reset and a fresh builder relaunched with the critic's blocking issues plus the iteration-1 commit body. Iteration 2 passed (5/5/4/5). The critic's remaining suggestions (e_driver->q edge grazing h_mig, t_oai cone over the tests caption, paired polarity signs at edge crossings, long e_pay->h_wage edge) are cosmetic and left as-is. Engine note from the builder: snap.mjs measures .nlabel rects before the inner .lab translateY(11px), so its overlap metric is about 11px off what a reader sees. Reconcile: README synced to the 34 labels shortened by the viz builders (texts, confidences, quotes and idea fields already matched exactly); content diff against the scaffold commit with layout fields and labels stripped is identical; all relative links and the wikipedia link resolve; validate 0/0.
Final review: edge x5 source_ref said 'hosts' but L328-L330 is one speaker's turn; changed to 'host' in graph.json and README.

blocking_issues: Band borders run through the node-label rows in both examples: CSS2D labels render about 5 world units below the node centre, but several node rows sit only 4-5 units above their band's lower bound, so the label lands in the seam between two regions and the rule reads as struck through the text. Leave at least 7 world units between a band's lowest node row and that band's lower bound.

In the tbpn example h_blind and h_comp sit directly beneath an issue that is not their parent (h_blind under i_iaas though its parent is i_meas; h_comp under i_supply though its parent is i_iaas), and the same drift repeats one layer down with t_mig under h_comp and t_gpu under h_pilot. No hypothesis or test may sit within about 4 world units of the x of an unrelated parent directly above it.
suggestions: Rightmost labels overhang the right edge of their region rectangle onto the background (classic i_use, h_empty, t_empty, e_dead; tbpn t_pilot): widen the region x extents or pull the rightmost column in.
The grounding view is nearly indistinguishable from the default at this density; engine styling rather than a page fault.
The hover tooltip floats over the side panel in both panel screenshots; probably the snap harness leaving the cursor on the clicked node.
The facts-only views are the strongest thing on the page and should be protected through any layout change.
viz_reviews.summary: Five provenance-labelled bands running Question to Issues to Hypotheses to Tests to Evidence, each captioned with its stated/added split, so hiding derived empties the issue layer and strips tests to nothing (classic) or one lone solid cone (tbpn). Counts match graph.json, panels correct, console clean, zero label overlaps. Two concrete layout defects: band borders cut through label rows, and in tbpn four nodes sit under a parent that is not theirs.

suggestions: tbpn: the solid fact edge e_driver -> q (bears_on) runs almost exactly through h_mig at pos [0,-6] ('Firms go to cloud for AI'); with derived hidden it reads as if 'Core infra drove the 39%' were joined to h_mig. Shift h_mig to about x=-15 (or e_driver to x=-20) so the line clears the sphere.

tbpn: the band header 'TESTS — 1 STATED, 7 ADDED' is partly covered by the t_oai cone at pos [-11,-26]; lowering t_oai to y=-30 (or raising the tests region top from -17 to -15) would uncover the '1 STATED'.

tbpn: the bears_on sign labels for x26/x27 ('+ +' near x=-33,y=-30) and x29/x30 ('- +' near x=55,y=-32) sit as adjacent pairs where the edges cross, so it is hard to tell which sign belongs to which edge; a small x offset of e_m365 or e_chatgpt would separate the crossing points.
classic (cosmetic): the e_pay -> h_wage fact edge crosses the whole Tests band; moving e_pay from x=-35 to x=15 would make it a short near-vertical line under h_wage.
viz_reviews.summary: The plane layout renders the tree as five colour-coded, labelled bands (Question / Issues / Hypotheses / Tests / Evidence) whose captions state the fact/derived tally of each slot, so the framework's shape is unmistakable and the provenance story is visible without any toggling. Facts-only is the strongest view: the Issues band empties completely and the Tests band keeps only the single stated test, which is exactly the framework's point (sources volunteer explanations, not MECE structure or falsifiers). Derived nodes show halo rings, dashed edges and the idea-bearing hypotheses (h_blind, h_pilot) carry the gold ring and star and open a panel with the opportunity block. Stats line matches graph.json for both examples (18 nodes / 25 edges and 26 nodes / 36 edges, grounding counted separately), panels show quote plus reference for facts and rationale plus confidence plus supporting facts for inferences, console clean, zero overlapping, off-screen or under-card labels in both examples. Remaining issues are minor edge/decor grazes in the TBPN example, listed as suggestions.
